 Live .  5,551 viewing 5551 viewing Live page Updated 1 minute ago Schools encourage pupils not to skip class after GTA 6 global release
 Summary
 Grand Theft Auto 6 has been released around the world, ending the 13-year wait for a new instalment of the game
 Wondering what the fuss is about? Tinshui Yeung explains all... 
 In the UK, some gamers found it hard to go to bed after the long-awaited midnight release 
 "I have to be up for work in five hours," one gamer told us overnight . "Why am I playing a game I have years to enjoy?"
 Meanwhile, schools are telling gamers not to skip class - with one school in Essex holding a raffle to stop pupils bunking off 
 GTA 6, in which players explore a fictional US state called Leonida, features the series' first playable female protagonist in a 3D setting
 And the reviews are very positive - "Great graphics and gameplay so far," one gamer in Newport says
 Close form Are you playing GTA 6? Tell us what you think!

 Live Reporting
 Edited by Tinshui Yeung, with Joe Coughlan reporting from Leonida
 In-game radio stations become portal to music discovery, says broadcaster published at 12:16 GMT 12:16 GMT 
 Jordan Kenny 
BBC Newsbeat 
 Image source, Rockstar Games Even if you're not into the game, one thing you'll be seeing and hearing is music from the soundtrack, which features huge artists including PinkPantheress, Bad Bunny and Cardi B.
 Players can flick through the in-game radio stations, each with a distinct playlist curated by some of the biggest names in the industry, including Robyn, Burna Boy and Lana Del Rey.
 Radio 1Xtra CassKidd has put together a special programme about GTA’s music. He says radio stations mean "the entry point to discovery through a video game is next level".
 The broadcaster says he was introduced to the likes of LA rapper Ice Cube through the last GTA, which "put me on a lot of rap music and music that I wasn’t listening growing up".
 "The way they merged alongside the real world is really nice and really particular."

 Expert concerns over 'widening gap' between winners and losers in gaming industry published at 11:48 GMT 11:48 GMT 
 Madeleine Lake 
Live reporter 
 Image source, Stephanie Farnsworth University lecturer Stephanie Farnsworth says the success of GTA 6 could set a standard that some games will struggle to reach.
 She says that a lot of games have promised huge open worlds but failed to deliver, and had to scale back in the end.
 Many studios will not be able to compete with the new standard Rockstar has set, she says, so they may need to start thinking about designing smaller worlds with unique features.
 Farnsworth is also concerned about the widening gap in the games industry between studios that produce blockbusters and those that face layoffs when targets are not met.
 "This does come at a huge time of cuts and layoffs in the last 18-24 months, including BioWare closing , which has been going for some decades.
 "If you're not a huge top dog, you're at risk in this climate."

 'It's a dream come true' - South African DJ celebrates featuring in GTA 6 published at 11:33 GMT 11:33 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images South African DJ Lag says it is a "dream come true" to have his music featured on GTA 6.
 DJ lag, one of South Africa's best-known electronic music producers, is among several African stars to feature, alongside Nigerian singers Burna Boy and Asake.
 "I can't explain the feeling. I started playing the game last night and it's amazing," DJ Lag told the BBC's Newsday programme, adding that he had been playing GTA since he was about 10 years old and could hardly believe he was now part of the latest edition.
 Read more about DJ Lag in our news story

 GTA 6 release generates more social media posts than start of 2026 World Cup - monitor firm published at 11:20 GMT 11:20 GMT 
 The launch of GTA 6 has reportedly generated more than 2.6 million posts on social media in 24 hours, according to social media monitor Visibrain.
 About 1,850 messages about the game were published per minute - 7% more than the number of posts at the start of the 2026 Fifa World Cup, the company tells AFP news agency.

 Who voices Lucia and Jason in GTA 6? published at 11:13 GMT 11:13 GMT 
 Image source, Anadolu via Getty Images Manni L Perez was thought to be voicing Lucia Caminos after being nominated for best performance at The Game Awards 2026 - one of eight nominations GTA 6 received.
 This was seemingly confirmed by her cousin on Instagram, who posted a picture with the actress and wrote: "From family to the big screen... couldn’t be prouder of you."
 According to her IMDb profile, Perez has also appeared in Law & Order: Special Victims Unit, Chicago PD and the Marvel TV series Jessica Jones. She also has credits for voicing minor roles in GTA 5 and GTA Online.
 It’s less clear who voices Jason Duval.
 A review by IGN Netherlands named Dylan Rourke as playing the role, but the article has since been changed to remove his name.
 Rourke has also remained silent on social media about his involvement in the game, following speculation from fans and gamers.
 According to IMDb, he has appeared in several films and TV series, including Grey's Anatomy, Modern Family, Send It! and Station 19.

 Police in GTA 6 remember your appearance and vehicle published at 11:00 GMT 11:00 GMT 
 Joe Coughlan 
Reporting from Leonida 
 Image caption, My questionable driving has left its mark on Jason's beloved '70 Ganado
 Spoiler alert: This post contains a few details about the game. 
 Driving in GTA has always been a touchy subject for me, so much so that, seconds after getting my old clunker repaired at the mechanic, I clipped a police car.
 I got out of my vehicle at the officer’s request, but he quickly escalated the exchange by punching Jason - prompting me to hit back and jump into my getaway vehicle.
 The chase was on. Police in GTA 6 remember details such as your outfit and vehicle, meaning you have to go home and change your clothes to help clear your wanted status.
 Later, my dodgy driving even tore a branch off a nearby tree as I was leaving a gift shop. Before I could feel any remorse, the limb despawned - breaking me out of my sun-soaked gaming reverie.

 WATCH: Family signs 'non-interruption' contract so fan can play GTA published at 10:40 GMT 10:40 GMT 
 Superfan Sean Little has made his wife and daughter sign a "non-interference contract" so he can play the new Grand Theft Auto in peace.
 Little's family are bound by the contract to spare him any household chores or dad duties for a week.
 He’s going to need it, with early reviews of the game suggesting it could take more than 80 hours to beat.
 Here's more about that contract in case you want to learn from him

 School says pupils should not 'be disengaged from their learning' for GTA 6 published at 10:25 GMT 10:25 GMT 
 Catriona Aitken 
BBC Wales 
 Birchgrove Comprehensive School in Swansea, south Wales, has warned parents and carers that despite “considerable excitement” around GTA 6, school studies should remain a priority.
 “The release of a new computer game should not be a reason for pupils to miss school, arrive late or be disengaged from their learning,” the school says.
 It adds it is aware of many conversations among pupils about the release, but it is “vital that all pupils are in school”.
 “Every school day matters, and we expect pupils to be present, punctual and ready to learn.”

 Rockstar's attention to detail includes... (spoiler below) published at 10:11 GMT 10:11 GMT 
 Joe Coughlan 
Reporting from Leonida 
 Image caption, Joe (left) pictured with Jason resting between sets at his home gym
 Spoiler alert: This post contains a few details about the game. 
 The first hour of GTA 6 includes a variety of engaging gameplay elements, with players encouraged to outrun police, dive into water and sneak through a compound during a stealth sequence.
 The ability to turn the heads-up display on and off adds to the cinematic feel.
 Cal, Jason's delirious friend, is already a source of comic relief, not unlike Lamar and Trevor in GTA 5 or Big Smoke in San Andreas.
 The attention to detail extends beyond the main story, with a fully interactive home gym and the ability to feed a pet snake. I can count 22 radio stations in Jason's notoriously difficult-to-operate muscle car.

 GTA 6 is a world within a world where normality co-exists with frenetic missions published at 10:00 GMT 10:00 GMT 
 Zoe Kleinman 
Technology and AI editor 
 Image source, Rockstar Games Christmas has come early for millions of gamers around the world as GTA 6 launches.
 Players have waited a long time for this - some of GTA's biggest fans were young children in 2013 when the last instalment came out. I was pregnant back then - and that baby is now a teenager.
 GTA 6 gets a universal thumbs up from all who have entered the fictional world of Leonida so far, as seen through the eyes of the game's two protagonists, Jason and Lucia.
 Grand Theft Auto has long had a reputation for being dark, violent and X-rated - and the franchise has definitely not mellowed with age. It's still an 18 for good reason.
 But you can also shop, fish and even watch GTA 6's very own TV shows within the game: it is a world within a world where normality also exists alongside the frenetic missions and criminal heists.
 And there's an added dimension now: players also control the relationship between Jason and Lucia. There's even a button to press to make them hold hands.

 'It feels like a life simulation,' says gamer in Germany published at 09:49 GMT 09:49 GMT 
 Image source, Timur Spoiler alert: This post contains a few details about the game. 
 Gamer Timur, from Germany, is among those playing GTA 6. He’s been impressed by how lifelike the game is.
 "It really feels like a life simulation with the amount of in-game encounters," he tells the BBC.
 During one interaction at a petrol station, Timur explains, a man was filling a bathtub with petrol. When asked what he was doing, "he got angry and sprayed gasoline all over me and spilled some on himself".
 "He was laughing at me, and while he was laughing, his leg caught fire. He put it out. My character chuckled, the guy insulted me and drove away."
 Image source, Timur

 Former Rockstar director explains why people love GTA 6 published at 09:36 GMT 09:36 GMT 
 Obbe Vermeij, former technical director at Rockstar North, has been staying up late to play the game.
 He says what's noteworthy about GTA 6 is the production value. 
 "There's about 2,000 people just on that one game for about eight years, so the production values now are just incredible," Obbe tells the BBC's Wake Up to Money programme from Ottawa, Canada.
 "You can go into that game, there's a beautiful city, beautiful people, cars, everything. There's tons of stuff to do. You have mini games, you can play basketball, you can play golf. There's actual video games within the video game," he explains. 
 "It's just nuts, the amount of stuff that there is to do. That's pretty much why people love it so much," he adds.

 How does saving in GTA 6 work? published at 09:23 GMT 09:23 GMT 
 Joe Coughlan 
Reporting from Leonida 
 Some gamers have expressed concern about saving their progress in GTA 6.
 Players can pause the game during open-world sections and save manually by going to the “game” section and selecting “save game”. 
 There is an autosave feature, but keeping a manual save file is a safe backup.

 GTA 6 breaks Virgin Media O2 broadband record as players download game published at 09:17 GMT 09:17 GMT 
 Image source, Getty Images Virgin Media O2 says the launch of GTA 6 has broken its evening traffic record for the second time this month.
 Traffic on its broadband network between 20:00 and 22:00 GMT - ahead of the game’s midnight release in the UK - was 9.4% higher than the previous record, set during pre-loading on 10 November, according to the provider.
 GTA 6 is download-only and requires up to 212 GB of available storage on consoles.

 She bought him a game voucher, he bought her a 'getaway basket' published at 09:05 GMT 09:05 GMT 
 Madeleine Lake 
Live reporter 
 Image source, Matildarose Nevin Matildarose Nevin was given a GTA “getaway basket” by her boyfriend Ryan, filled with many of her favourite things.
 The 22-year-old says Ryan didn’t want her to feel left out while he played the game, so he put together a selection of Lego, colouring books, pyjamas and self-care items.
 She says it was “thoughtful” because she doesn’t like video games but still wanted to spend time with him.
 Matildarose bought Ryan a £90 PlayStation voucher so he could buy the game.
 “He was really happy, he didn't think I'd get him it. We are all allowed our own hobbies and I'm excited for him to play it.”
 Image source, Matildarose Nevin She posted a video of her basket on TikTok, which she says has prompted some surprising reactions, including comments about cheating.
 The game's launch has sparked a debate about whether it's possible to cheat on someone with a video game character.
 Matildarose says it isn't: "It's fake, it's just pixels on a screen."
 Ryan has booked the day of the launch off, so the two will have a long weekend together.

 In pictures: Grand Theft Auto 6 adverts on display across the world published at 08:51 GMT 08:51 GMT 
 Posters for Grand Theft Auto 6 have gone on display around the world to mark its release.
 Large posters advertising the game have appeared in London's Piccadilly Circus, New York's Times Square and Tokyo's Akihabara Electric Town.
 Meanwhile, posters line a street in Hong Kong, and a tram has been covered from head to toe in the game's branding.

 'It's about time': Content creator reacts to GTA 6's female lead published at 08:40 GMT 08:40 GMT 
 Joe Coughlan 
Reporting from Leonida 
 Image source, CosyAurora CosyAurora, a UK-based gaming content creator, has taken four days of annual leave for the launch of GTA 6.
 She says "it's about time" the series introduced a female lead in its modern 3D and HD format.
 The 26-year-old tells me: "Women have always gamed. We have just never really had the representation."
 "It's been a long time coming and it's something that sort of needs to happen in gaming," she adds.
 She describes the move as "huge", if not slightly overdue. While it won't make women forget how they were depicted in the GTA series in the past, she says it's an overall net positive and "refreshing" to see.

 Why are people complaining about frame rate – and what is it? published at 08:25 GMT 08:25 GMT 
 Tom Gerken 
Technology reporter 
 If you’re not particularly nerdy about gaming, you may have been left a bit confused by all the chatter about FPS - frames per second, also known as frame rate.
 As the name suggests, it’s the number of still frames a game displays per second. But really, it’s all about smoothness.
 Things look smoother at higher frame rates, so while a game running at 30 FPS looks great, one at 60 FPS is ultra-smooth. Some people with very powerful PCs even play games at 120 FPS.
 So, with higher frame rates now the standard, there’s been noticeable disappointment that GTA 6 is limited to just 30 FPS, which seems a bit archaic.
 In truth, most people won’t notice this. But it does mean the game isn’t as smooth as it could be, because it’s simply too demanding on modern hardware.
 And if you too are seething with jealousy that my colleague Joe gets to play the game , I’m with you - I’ll have to wait until this evening, like many of you reading this!

 Crisp graphics show character's pores against the neon world of Leonida published at 08:13 GMT 08:13 GMT 
 Joe Coughlan 
Reporting from Leonida 
 Spoiler alert: This post contains a few details about the game. 
 I was pleasantly surprised when I first booted up GTA 6 not to be greeted by a further download, after Sony warned PlayStation users that an update would be required before they could play the game.
 The game's prologue provides backstory for the protagonists, Jason and Lucia, as well as a lush advertisement for its sprawling world, with neon lights, swimming pools and aeroplanes.
 Transitions between cutscenes and gameplay are seamless. The graphics are so crisp in places that you can see the pores on characters' faces and individual hairs bouncing as they walk.
 However, I did notice a slight drop in frame rate during an early chase scene following a robbery. It's a flaw already being pointed out in early reviews of the game, but it could also be because I'm playing on an Xbox Series S, Microsoft's budget version of the flagship Series X console.
 Despite this, the world feels incredibly vibrant as you cut through the water in a speedboat beneath the Leonida sun - in stark contrast to the dark backdrop of the UK on a November morning.
 What is frame rate? We'll tell you more about that in our next post

 'I don't think anyone could have imagined the success of the series,' says GTA 3 artist published at 08:07 GMT 08:07 GMT 
 Freya Scott-Turner 
Live reporter 
 Image source, Bloomberg via Getty Images Image caption, Bliss was behind the iconic cover designs of GTA 3 and Vice City
 "I love the new artwork, it's amazing," says Stephen Bliss. He's the artist behind GTA 3's iconic cover and worked on the later games up to GTA 5.
 "I don't think anyone could have imagined the success [of the GTA series]," he says, speaking to me from New York.
 His GTA 3 cover became something of a blueprint for the series, which has replicated the comic strip style in all subsequent games. But it wasn't plain sailing making it.
 "I'd finished painting [the original cover], it took a long time and then 9/11 happened," he explains. "That was terrifying."
 He remembers thinking: "There's no way there will ever be suggestions of violence [in video games] again."
 So he got to work designing new artwork, removing all the violent images, guns and explosions.
 And the result was the cover we know today.
